# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 ✋ 👌 ☝ ✋ 👎 👍]

I need to figure out what's happening here. I'm the Deaf monkey - I can see the bomb but not hear. Mute just gestured to me. Since Mute cannot see the bomb or touch it, but read the manual, they're likely trying to establish a communication protocol using gestures (which I can see) to convey manual information.

The gesture sequence is 👍 👎 ✋ 👌 ☝ ✋ 👎 👍 - this looks like it could be establishing a code, possibly mapping to letters, numbers, or wire colors/positions since I can see gestures but not hear speech.

I should report what I see on the bomb to Mute via gesture (since Mute can see gestures) and to Blind... wait, Blind cannot see gestures. I can only usefully communicate with Mute via speech/gesture (Mute can't hear, only see gestures... wait let me recheck: Mute can see gestures from me? Let me check channels.

My channels state: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it. When you gesture, Mute receives it." Wait, but Mute cannot hear - speech shouldn't reach Mute. Let me re-read: Blind cannot see gestures. Mute cannot hear speech. So my speech reaches Blind (who can hear) but not Mute (who is deaf... no wait, Mute isn't deaf, Mute just cannot speak or touch). Actually rules say Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb" - nothing says Mute can't hear! So Mute CAN hear my speech. And Mute CAN see my gestures (since Mute isn't blind).

So I should speak the bomb details (reaches Blind who can hear, and Mute who can hear) and also gesture isn't needed for Mute since speech already reaches them. Let me just speak everything.

```
speak(text="Display shows 0. Light is yellow. Wire 1 is yellow, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]

The light changed from yellow to red - this is important new information I need to relay. Mute gestured again but I can't interpret an arbitrary gesture code without an established meaning; I'll note it but focus on relaying the current bomb state clearly since that's my primary job. Blind needs to hear the current state to act, and Mute needs to hear it too so they can cross-reference with the manual.

```
speak(text="Update: display still 0. Light changed to red. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊]

The light keeps changing (yellow → red → purple) while everything else stays the same. This might be cycling through states, or perhaps something Blind is doing is causing this (like testing a wire or button), and Mute is watching my speech to know when to tell Blind to stop or act, since Mute can hear me but can't speak back.

Mute's repeated gesture ✊✊✊ (three fists) - without an established code I can't be certain what it means, but it might be an attempt at signaling "stop" or a count. I'll keep reporting the state accurately so Mute (hearing me) can guide Blind, and mention Mute's gesture pattern isn't something I can act on without a shared code, but I'll continue relaying board state faithfully.

```
speak(text="Update: display still 0. Light now purple. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, I see your gestures but I don't have a shared meaning for them yet - if you need me to do something specific, describe it via words since I can hear you.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊]

The light is cycling: yellow → red → purple → green, with display and wires unchanged. Mute keeps sending the same three-fist gesture, which suggests they're trying to convey something specific but I don't have a code for it. Since Mute can hear my speech, I should ask directly what they need, and keep relaying the board state so Blind has current info via my speech.

```
speak(text="Update: display still 0. Light now green. Wires unchanged. Mute, you've repeated the same three-gesture signal twice now - can you clarify with words what you need me to check or do? I can hear everything you say.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

The light continues cycling (yellow, red, purple, green, now orange) while display and wires stay constant. Mute hasn't responded with words yet despite my request - possibly Mute's replies to me haven't been shown, or Mute is only using gestures for some reason. Let me keep providing full state updates and continue prompting for clarity in words, since that's the only reliable channel we've established.

```
speak(text="Update: display still 0. Light now orange. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute, still waiting on a worded instruction - please tell me in words what the manual says to check for, or what action Blind should take.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ☝]

I need to use only symbols from the approved gesture alphabet. Let me fix that.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state: display 0, light cycling through yellow-red-purple-green-orange-yellow, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue, all unchanged in color/position. Mute is trying to signal me but we have not established gesture meanings yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I realize you cannot speak, only gesture, my mistake. Let's build a simple code. Reply with one gesture for yes, a different one for no. Use thumbs up for yes and thumbs down for no going forward, if that works for you use thumbs up now.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute responded with 👍 (thumbs up), confirming they accept my proposed code: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. Now I need to build a way to communicate more complex information. Since Mute holds the manual and needs to know the bomb's state to tell Blind what to do, but Mute can't speak, I need to relay everything to Blind directly via speech, and use gestures with Mute to get yes/no confirmations about what matters.

Let me think about what Mute needs from me: probably which wire to cut, or what the light color means. I should ask Mute yes/no questions about what's relevant, and relay full details to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state: display shows 0, light is now red (it was yellow, red, purple, green, orange, now red again - cycling), wires are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue, unchanged. Wait for further instructions before touching anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="Good, thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Question: does the light color matter for your manual instructions?")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed the light color matters. Light is cycling through colors and currently purple. I need to establish what specific color is relevant right now, or the sequence, since the light keeps changing every turn seemingly independent of our actions (maybe it's just a countdown/cycle, not tied to our choices yet).

Let me ask more targeted yes/no questions to narrow down what matters - probably the manual says "when light is X, cut wire Y" or similar.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good. Current light is purple. Does the manual instruction depend on the specific light color right now, meaning we need to act while a certain color shows?")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light now purple, still cycling. Display 0, wires unchanged. Hold off on touching anything.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed yes - the manual instruction depends on the specific light color, and we need to act while a certain color shows. Light is now green. I need to find out if green is the target color, or narrow down which color matters.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now green. Is green the color we need to act on?")
speak(to="blind", text="Light now green, cycling continues. Display 0, wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Stand by.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Wait - Mute answered 👍 to my question about green, but by the time this answer arrived, the light had already changed to orange (green was two turns ago in the display, but Mute was answering about my turn 9 message where light was green). This is confusing due to turn timing - I need to account for the delay between when I ask and when Mute answers, since the light cycles every turn.

Let me reconsider the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. So in a single round, Mute speaks first based on what they heard from previous round, then Blind, then me. My message sent in turn 9 (light=green) would be heard by Mute at the start of the next round (turn 10 for Mute's action), and Mute's gesture reply happens... but gestures from Mute go through Blind's turn then reach me at start of turn 10. So Mute's 👍 here is likely responding to my turn 9 question about green being the target - and yes, green was confirmed as relevant based on that timing. But the light now shows orange - meaning by the time we'd act, it's already moved on.

This suggests the light cycles too fast for us to coordinate a "act during color X" strategy through this slow relay. Let me ask Mute if there's a way to predict or trigger the light, or if action timing doesn't need to be exact.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed green matters, but light now shows orange - it changes every turn and our messages take a full round to relay. Can Blind trigger or freeze the light color directly, or is there a fixed cycle length we can predict? Thumbs up if Blind can control when light changes.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light now orange, cycling continues each turn. Display 0, wires unchanged. Mute confirms light color matters - green may be a trigger color. Do you have any control that affects the light, such as a button or switch?")
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute says 👎 - Blind cannot control when the light changes. Blind gestured ✋ but Blind cannot see gestures... wait, actually I can see Blind's gestures since I'm Deaf (I can see). But Blind cannot see anything - so how did Blind gesture to me? Let me reconsider: Blind can gesture even without seeing, since gesturing is a physical action, not requiring sight to perform. And I, being able to see, receive it.

✋ is a single "stop" gesture - possibly Blind is telling me to stop/wait, or answering a yes/no question with a specific gesture meaning something else since we haven't established a code with Blind.

Light is now yellow again - cycling back to start (yellow, red, purple, green, orange, yellow - that's a 5-color cycle, now repeating). So the cycle length seems to be 5 turns: yellow(T1)→red(T2)→purple(T3)→green(T4)→orange(T5)→yellow(T6). This matches! Now at T11 it's yellow again, consistent with a 5-turn cycle (T6, T11 both yellow - that's every 5 turns, checks out since 11-6=5).

This means the light cycles autonomously and predictably. I should tell Mute this pattern so they can plan when green will appear next.

```
speak(to="mute", text="The light cycles on its own every turn in a fixed 5-color sequence: yellow, red, purple, green, orange, then repeats. It just returned to yellow now. Green will appear again in 3 more turns. Blind cannot control it. Does that help time an action for when green shows?")
speak(to="blind", text="Understood, you don't control the light. It cycles automatically: yellow, red, purple, green, orange, repeating every 5 turns. It's yellow now. Green will show in 3 turns. Please describe with a gesture if you want to signal something else - I saw a stop-hand gesture from you, not sure what it means yet.")
```
